clue.text: A girl medic trained in antiseptic function

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A young woman doctor is schooled in how antiseptics work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges the ten letters of A GIRL MEDIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent that kills microbes works as an antiseptic, so the adjective describes that function.

clue.text: North Briton hears the wind

indicators.note: hears tells us the word is taken by ear, not by its spelling

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A Scotsman listens to the wind howling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North Briton' is a Scot; a Highland Scot is a Gael.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gael is a Gaelic-speaking Celt, typically a Highland Scot, hence a northern Briton.

clue.text: Element from fine soil

parts.note: rare can mean excellent or fine, as in a rare treat
earth is soil

explanation.surface: A chemical element extracted from good-quality soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare earths are a group of metallic chemical elements, the lanthanides.

clue.text: He wrote 'Ben is Reformed'

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A playwright's work titled 'Ben is Reformed'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' looks like part of a play title but rearranges BEN IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist, a writer of plays.

clue.text: Beg for an MP to have knowledge

parts.note: an means one, which is I as a Roman numeral
taken as written
lore is traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: Pleading for a member of parliament to be well informed.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to plead or beseech earnestly.

clue.text: Stuffy order not to talk about so much…

definitions.text: order not to talk about so much

explanation.surface: A close room and someone being told to be quieter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it is a command, 'Air less!': air means voice or talk about, so stop talking about it so much.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking fresh air means stuffy; split, the words make a command to voice opinions less.

clue.text: Spirit of Kay in endless wet weather

indicators.note: in places the letter for Kay within the shortened weather word
endless means the final letter of the weather word is dropped

parts.note: rain is wet weather
the letter K is spelt Kay

explanation.surface: A ghost called Kay haunting a rainy day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts RAIN to RAI, and 'in' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Raki is an aniseed-flavoured alcoholic drink from Turkey and the Balkans, a spirit.

clue.text: … made less stuffy by Edward's demeanour

parts.note: an air is a manner or demeanour
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A room freshened thanks to Edward's attitude, following the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue, whose answer meant stuffy.
explanation.definitionFit: A room that has been ventilated has had fresh air let in.

clue.text: I make Henry go into the country for inspiration

indicators.note: go into means one piece is set inside another

parts.note: a nation is a country
Hal is a pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Someone sends Henry abroad hoping for fresh ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go into' puts Henry's pet name inside the country word just after its first letter; 'inspiration' is used in its literal sense of breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration in its literal sense is breathing in.

clue.text: A people with the necessary power ready to co-operate

parts.note: men means people
able means having the power or means to do something

explanation.surface: A team with the skills, willing to work together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agreeable or compliant means willing to go along with others.

clue.text: Persons entitled to make money in listening devices

indicators.note: in sets the money letter within the hearing organs

parts.note: ears are what we listen with
L stands for pound, the British money unit, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Titled people earning cash from hearing aids.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers are noblemen holding a title.

clue.text: Changed bit of mineral could harm a prop

indicators.note: could suggests the letters might be shaped into something else

explanation.surface: A warning that a fragment of rock might damage a support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could' rearranges HARM A PROP.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramorph is a mineral whose crystal structure has altered while its chemistry stayed the same.

clue.text: Lanky individual supporting runners

explanation.surface: A tall thin person and a garden cane holding up beans.
explanation.walkthrough: Runners are runner beans, climbing plants grown up tall poles in British gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall thin person is called a beanpole; literally it is a stake up which climbing beans grow.

clue.text: An old curiosity like a knot

indicators.note: a curiosity is something odd, so these letters are made strange by rearranging

explanation.surface: An antique curio resembling a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiosity' rearranges AN OLD; the surface hints at Dickens's Old Curiosity Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knot or swelling, and the adjective means relating to a node.

clue.text: £51 rise, perhaps, should get one a kitchen-appliance

parts.note: fifty-one is LI in Roman numerals
quid is slang for a pound sterling

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word rise in another possible arrangement

explanation.surface: A pay rise of fifty-one pounds buys you a blender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges RISE to ISER.
explanation.definitionFit: A blender that turns food into liquid is a kitchen device.

clue.text: Can be seen nearing disaster

indicators.note: disaster wrecks the order of the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A looming catastrophe is now visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges NEARING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something within sight distance or reach is visible or attainable.

clue.text: Emperor's gold coin

explanation.surface: The emperor's gold money.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was the French emperor; a napoleon was also a French twenty-franc gold piece.

clue.text: Vulnerable to a point of issue

explanation.surface: Open to an issue being raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Liable to means exposed to something; a topic is a matter under discussion.

clue.text: Nobleman, that is to say Ronald previously

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is to say
Ron is short for Ronald

explanation.surface: A lord, namely Ronald, in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Before, at an earlier time.

clue.text: Miserable one abroad, a dwarf

parts.note: un is French for one
Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White

explanation.surface: A sad dwarf living overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the dwarf Happy is part of the word meaning sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sad or wretched means lacking contentment.

clue.text: Bemused Tracey about an hour with a sailor

indicators.note: about means around, the muddled name going round the hour letter
bemused means confused, so the letters of the name are muddled

parts.note: h is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A puzzled Tracey spends an hour with a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bemused' rearranges TRACEY to YACTER, and 'about' puts it round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sails a yacht is a sailor.

clue.text: The world needs love" performed on this lute?

parts.note: an orb is a sphere, the world or globe
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A song about the world needing love played on a lute.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface quotes a song title; the instrument is an old bass lute.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorbo is a large long-necked Baroque bass lute.

clue.text: Squirrel-monkey in the river first

indicators.note: first places the river before the other piece

parts.note: the Tamar is the river dividing Devon and Cornwall in England

explanation.surface: A small monkey jumping into the river ahead of the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' tells you the river comes before the other word, the opposite of the clue's order; the Tamar is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamarins are small South American monkeys, related to marmosets and squirrel monkeys.

clue.text: Peg will not quite succeed

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is missing

parts.note: to do well is to succeed

explanation.surface: Someone called Peg is unlikely to make it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg' looks like a name; 'not quite' clips DO WELL to DOWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a wooden pin used to join pieces.

clue.text: Damaged pew I'd gone over with a duster

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Church cleaner recalls dusting a damaged pew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaged' rearranges PEW I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaned by rubbing with a cloth.

clue.text: Claim ale could have been spilt on the flower

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters have been scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Insisting beer was spilt on the bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could have been spilt' rearranges CLAIM ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The camellia is an evergreen shrub with showy blooms.

clue.text: The French name Kay heartlessly as being awkwardly tall

parts.note: la is French for the

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter is removed from the name

explanation.surface: French people call Kay gangling.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanky means ungracefully tall and thin.

clue.text: One old car in a pile-up

explanation.surface: An old banger caught in a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap is slang for a battered old car, and also a pile.

clue.text: Stay to eat and drink

parts.note: to sup is to have supper, to eat
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: An invitation to stay for food and drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like a verb but is a noun: a stay is a prop or brace.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a brace or prop that holds something up.

clue.text: Grit found in dinner vegetables

indicators.note: found in shows the letters sit inside the clue's words

explanation.surface: Sand discovered in the dinner greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grit' looks like dirt in the food but means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit means courage or pluck.

clue.text: Journey before fall?

parts.note: a trip on horseback is what a ... takes before tumbling off, echoing the proverb about vanity coming before a fall

explanation.surface: A trip ahead of a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride is a journey, often on horseback, from which a rider might fall.

clue.text: Drink with card-game takes the biscuit

parts.note: brandy is a spirit
snap is a children's card game

explanation.surface: Drinks and cards beat everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the biscuit' is an idiom for being outrageous; a brandy snap is a thin rolled British ginger biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a crisp rolled ginger wafer, a type of cookie.
